Making the background color obnoxiously dark isn't going to accomplish that, and there are a few reasons for that.

1) The average person prefers and is used to a white background screen. Look at practically every website that relies on online presence--news outlets, social media, etc. They all use a white background because it's neutral, upbeat, and what people are used to. Websites with dark backgrounds or cheesy colors are usually seen as unprofessional.

2) A lot of people who use Voat may be using it at work or somewhere else that they might not necessarily want to advertise that they're relaxing, or using a website that's most known for things like FPH. Having a black background just screams to everyone around that you're doing that, it would stick out like a sore thumb.

3) Colors have an effect on mood and perception. Making the default color something so dark could make people perceive Voat as less cheerful, or dislike the experience. This is exactly why so many companies (which spend fortunes on market analysis) always choose light cheerful tones for their websites.

There's a difference between breaking the mold in a good way, and breaking established norms that have become established for a reason. Voat may want to change its color scheme and logo somewhere down the line, but just changing things over to "night" theme (which is I believe primarily for people who prefer energy saving options) isn't going to do it.

For people looking at Hatoful Boyfriend for the first time and are thinking, "wtf, Japan?" Let me tell you what many places fail to mention about the game.

Hatoful Boyfriend is a visual novel that parodies the highschool romance genre. For those who watch/read other entertainment stuff from Japan, it's the equivalent of Ouran High School Host Club (mocking shoujo/harem romance) or Cromartie High School (shounen street punks).

It's been years, but if I recall correctly when it first was released in Japan it was on April Fools. I also can't tell how many times I've bought this. Firstly as a fun quirky indie/doujin title, then the fact it actually came out in English, then an HD release???

I'm really happy it's doing well but I really wonder what other people who don't know what it's mocking are getting out of it. It's the equivalent of someone saying they enjoyed Galaxy Quest but they never watched Star Trek. So many important ques are missing! What are you laughing at?

For those who aren't into visual novels, this is hardly the what is considered the best of the medium. If you love surrealist parodies though, do check it out.
